# Pre-S2 origin export/restore fixtures

## Coverage and limits

All **141/141 policy-admitted named keys and28/28 named exclusions** in the
pinned S2-1..5 inventory are covered. Counts by domain (admitted/excluded):
S2-1 41/3; S2-2 30/10; S2-3 34/7; S2-4 28/0; S2-5 8/8. The141 includes four
conditional player selections and two explicit null-overlay fields.

All **five dynamic families have finite samples**, totaling21 distinct keys:
16 ordinary/empty-suffix keys, four always-excluded credential-shaped keys,
and one credential-shaped engine key admitted only when includeSecrets is true.
This does not cover every possible suffix, every legal value, all storage keys,
S2-6/7, resource graphs, encrypted account-secret migration, PIN/recovery,
platform integration or complete profile sync.

`recipe.json` is the exact key/value/type recipe and named-domain/family
inventory. Every named input belongs to exactly one declared complete domain;
the loader checks the141/28 partition and the21 separately enumerated family
samples. Each manifest records original exported values/types, scenario,
includeSecrets flag, absences/omissions and ciphertext hash. Assertions inspect
every represented key/value/type after actual restore and re-export. Completeness
metadata is supplementary; these are not source-text or copied-body behavioral
pins. Physical values include bool,int,double,String,List<String>. A manifest
null means an overlay removal, never a stored SharedPreferences null value.

## Origin and isolation

All seven packages were generated by actual unchanged production at
`6d26d7a1a98c7ddd37b4a25815f74123c1e29126`, immediately before S2-1 extraction
`c8c33ed8`. This does not retroactively make old extraction tests pre-move pins.
Generation checks exact HEAD, clean lib and package resolution to that checkout.
Real StorageService/ProfilePreferences writes feed ProfilePackageService export
and the real encrypted codec. No production source bodies are copied or edited.

Inputs and expected encodings are independent recipe data, not derived from the
candidate exporter. Named input writer types were checked against origin for
139keys; two legacy integer names (debrify_tv_keyword_threshold and
 debrify_tv_min_torrents_per_keyword) are covered by the origin characterization
fixture. Legacy prefix samples test physical preference transport, not the
presence of an active writer or every UI getter normalization.

Normal tests decrypt the frozen original bytes and restore through
ProfileRestoreCoordinator, inspect physical types before getters can coerce them,
exercise selected provider/tracking readers, and re-export. Old generations and
an unrelated profile retain their sentinels. Named exclusions plus four dynamic
exclusions are seeded/asserted present before export and stay excluded with both
includeSecrets values. The engine credential-shaped sample is separately checked
as omitted or included according to the source export flag.

All data is synthetic: mock SharedPreferences, temporary directories/registry,
in-memory device cipher, example.invalid URLs and obvious non-credential markers.
Network access is denied. No installed profile, working account credential or
real device key is read, copied or uploaded. Packages contain zero resources.
Testing credential-shaped preference names is not testing a real secret vault
or resource graph migration. The public fixture passphrase is intentionally in
the test. Normal tests never regenerate artifacts.

## Scenario semantics

- profile:157 exported entries (141 named including two nulls +16 family samples).
- provider-null-folder:154 entries. Actual null restricted-folder setter removes
  ID/name but retains cached subfolder IDs; null selected WebDAV ID is removed.
- provider-cleared-cache:152 entries. Actual clear operation also removes both
  subfolder caches; empty selected WebDAV ID is removed.
- player-custom, player-custom-app, player-custom-command:153 entries each.
  Together they cover every excluded selector spelling: external custom,
  custom_app, custom_command; iOS custom_scheme; Linux/Windows custom_command.
- family-secrets-included:158 entries, adding the synthetic credential-shaped
  engine preference when includeSecrets is true.

Omitted provider/player keys are tested in empty and populated destinations:
absence stays absent, while merge restore retains existing destination values.
In contrast, iptv_last_live_channel and startup_iptv_channel synthetic execution
strings export as explicit nulls. Restore removes stale destination values,
preserves old-generation values and re-exports neither cleared key. A null
overlay and an omitted preference are intentionally different contracts.

- `engine_tv_`: `engine_tv_`, `engine_tv_synthetic_alpha`, `engine_tv_synthetic_beta`, `engine_tv_synthetic_playback_ratio`; credential-shaped `engine_tv_synthetic_api_key`.
- `debrify_tv_use_`: `debrify_tv_use_`, `debrify_tv_use_synthetic_alpha`, `debrify_tv_use_synthetic_beta`; credential-shaped `debrify_tv_use_synthetic_api_key`.
- `debrify_tv_channel_small_`: `debrify_tv_channel_small_`, `debrify_tv_channel_small_synthetic_alpha`, `debrify_tv_channel_small_synthetic_beta`; credential-shaped `debrify_tv_channel_small_synthetic_api_key`.
- `debrify_tv_channel_large_`: `debrify_tv_channel_large_`, `debrify_tv_channel_large_synthetic_alpha`, `debrify_tv_channel_large_synthetic_beta`; credential-shaped `debrify_tv_channel_large_synthetic_api_key`.
- `debrify_tv_quick_play_`: `debrify_tv_quick_play_`, `debrify_tv_quick_play_synthetic_alpha`, `debrify_tv_quick_play_synthetic_beta`; credential-shaped `debrify_tv_quick_play_synthetic_api_key`.

Empty suffixes are the bare prefix names. Alpha/beta samples prove multiple
entries survive; the engine playback-ratio sample adds a double-valued setting.
The engine credential sample exports only with includeSecrets true. The four
other credential-shaped samples are excluded regardless of that flag. These21
keys are finite examples of five unbounded prefix families, not21 additional
named keys in the141 count.

and restore before the semantic assertions fail. No product source mutation.
Each following define must exit1 for the populated-profile restore case:


for final-domain probes. They respectively rename Reddit favorites, replace a

and player modes remain in the shared recipe; conditional/null insertion modes
need their documented matching scenario (provider-null-folder or player-custom).

## Residual domain: five default torrent filters

`filter-defaults.encrypted.json` adds a separately counted **5-key residual
preferences domain**. The original S2 inventory remains 141 admitted / 28 excluded
named keys and 21 finite family samples; this is not a 146-key completion claim.
The new scenario has no exclusions or resources. Existing encrypted files are unchanged.

The five keys are `default_filter_qualities_v1`, `default_filter_rip_sources_v1`,
`default_filter_languages_v1`, `default_filter_sizes_v1`, and
`default_filter_dynamic_ranges_v1`. Each is a physical **String containing JSON**,
not a SharedPreferences StringList. The independent residual recipe exercises
ordering, duplicates, unknown names, an empty string and non-ASCII text. Real
StorageService setters seed the actual pre-S2 exporter; current restore compares
all five raw types/JSON bytes before invoking the readers, then re-exports.
Previous-generation and unrelated-profile filter values, the destination's legacy
honors flag and both movie/series rule strings remain unchanged.

Export origin: `6d26d7a1a98c7ddd37b4a25815f74123c1e29126`.
Current behavioral origin: `ba527454bb69a6cebb6fc226ed075ee176b24b69`.
These are deliberately different: pre-S2 reset used one captured preferences
instance for all six removals. Current reset removes five filters on captured
preferences and then calls the provider store, which acquires preferences again.
The new 19-case behavioral pin preserves current semantics, including a profile
switch after the fifth filter clearing the **new** profile's provider. A switch
after the first filter instead rejects the stale instance before subsequent work.
It does not fix that behavior or claim it existed at the export origin.

The behavior tests cover all five absent defaults, exact setter/reader encoding,
malformed JSON, wrong JSON roots/elements and physical StringList errors; ordered
reset, failure at each of the six removals, and both held profile-switch points.
No product extraction, global cache, resource graph or complete-sync claim.

`test/default_torrent_filter_prefs_origin_test.dart` helper in the isolated

Keep the three `StorageService.clearAllFilterSettings` calls and every assertion
unchanged. This is a test-harness adapter to the actual old APIs, not a production
backport or an identical-harness claim; existing artifact bytes are unchanged.

### Residual playback repair: seven-key domain, three actual origin packages

Current test origin `84c6a130e82ce696b6d8dbc38e69dc27c584e77d`;
actual export origin `6d26d7a1a98c7ddd37b4a25815f74123c1e29126`.
This is test-only; no production/registry/bridge or CODEMAP change, zero Leaves.

The seven-key union is four physical ints (`movie_completion_threshold`,
`episode_completion_threshold`, `playback_completion_migration_generation`,
`resume_ghost_purge_generation`), String JSON `playback_state_v1`, String JSON
`continue_watching_v1`, and StringList `finished_movies_v1`.
`repair.encrypted.json` exports five keys with BOTH markers absent;
`repair-markers-zero.encrypted.json` exports seven with BOTH markers int0;
`repair-markers-one.encrypted.json` exports seven with BOTH markers int1.
Each has its own manifest and actual ciphertext SHA256. Seven distinct keys,
not nineteen distinct keys or a new blanket S2 inventory total.

The absence package's restore derives purge int0, but does not derive the
completion migration marker. That purge0 is NOT counted as exported. Presence,
physical type and absence are checked before any repair/defaulting. The recipe
contains independent exact input/sanitized/after-migration/after-purge JSON.
Actual exporter strips all eight execution field spellings represented by the
playlist fixture, including nested/list fields. No source URL/path/header bytes
are claimed portable and no real user secrets or network requests are used.

After actual current ProfileRestoreCoordinator restoration, assertions inspect
physical types and exact JSON and re-export the represented snapshot. Only THEN
are three SQLite resume rows seeded through actual StorageService APIs in the
test's isolated profile database. A before/after export comparison proves those
rows are not exported preferences. No resource graph or native claim.

Repair order is explicit: migrateExistingPlaybackCompletionThresholds, then
purgeUnwatchedResumeGhosts. Absent/zero cases finish the equal-threshold movie,
remove both IMDb-equivalent movie states and SQLite resumes, retain the partial
movie, finish the equal-threshold episode preserving updatedAt/finishedAt5,
then purge one unmarked zero-position ghost. False/null finished marks and the
0ms/1ms dummy shape survive. Stage snapshots capture the real revision boundary:
finished list changes before CW/playback/final migration marker; purge playback
changes before its final marker. One-marker packages skip BOTH repairs and keep
all original state/resume rows. Second runs produce no extra revision and retain
exact state. Destination sentinel, old generation and other profile remain intact.

Malformed inputs run as TWO SEPARATE negative incoming packages derived from the
real absent-marker export through actual section hashing/encryption: purge
marker String"1", and episode position String"75". Exact restored raw values are
asserted before the real repair throws TypeError; no revision or state change is
expected. These are derived negative packages, not extra frozen pre-S2 exports.
No normalization of marker/null/type or swallowed exception makes normal cases
pass. Mixed marker combinations, every malformed stage/interleaving, database
failure during fixture repair and device activation are not exhaustively covered;
PR150's separate origin pin covers finite SQLite failure/profile scheduling cases.

actual pre-S2 export origin `6d26d7a1a98c7ddd37b4a25815f74123c1e29126`.

`playlist_poster_overrides_v1`. Both are admitted physical Strings, and exact
JSON bytes (including whitespace, insertion order and nested scalar types) survive
actual current restore. No blanket S2 inventory increase is claimed.

Synthetic input has three mappings with fixed integer show IDs/timestamps and
three corresponding poster URLs at example.invalid. Additional empty/null poster
values and a nonmap record remain in raw JSON but are excluded by the actual
batch getter. Five public lookups cover RD integer/string identity collision,
normalized-title collision and WebDAV precedence/path case; each checks the real
unique-key, mapping and poster API. Batch output order and missing-item nulls are
also checked. These are finite cases, not network/image loading or native proof.

The existing generator runs against the actual origin library, checks its Git
HEAD and clean lib, verifies own package resolution, and uses the actual exporter
and encrypted package codec. Current restore uses the real coordinator and checks

`metadata_restore_sentinel` survive. Represented current re-export matches too.

snapshot policy excludes `tvmaze_` keys; this fixture does not change or prove that
